limitations_and_boundaries: The study focuses on immature mouse bone-marrow-derived dendritic cells; generalizability to other cell types or maturation states is not fully established.
The precise molecular mechanism by which actin assembly is triggered and the nuclear lamina is deformed requires further study.
Physical modeling and quantitative biophysical experiments are needed to fully test the proposed model.
The role of myosin II in passage through the smallest constrictions (1 µm) for neutrophils suggests additional mechanisms when the lamina is absent.
The study does not directly measure forces exerted by the perinuclear actin network.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.
